pitch_detail.notes: From the Clark-Johnson col, traverse ledges around the south side of the peak.
Continue the ledge traverse around the east side of the peak.
Short, exposed, loose finish up the north side of the summit block to the top.
Talus/heather traverse from Snowy Lakes to the west-face basin below the route.
Ledge system past a large cave (~20 ft tall) around the headwall blocking direct gully access.
Broad gully climbing for several hundred feet; stay right, don't exit early.
~15 ft of slabby climbing partway up the second gully; often wet; crux of the route.
Ledge system back to the ridge crest.
Exposed but moderate scramble along the ridge to the summit cairn.
3.5 miles, 2,800 ft gain, avalanche paths, ice axe may be needed early season
pitch_detail.pitch: 1: Easy Pass Trailhead to Easy Pass

pitch_detail.notes: 1.5 miles, 1,500 ft loss, scenic alpine to forest transition
pitch_detail.pitch: 2: Easy Pass to Fisher Creek valley

pitch_detail.notes: 0.5-1 mile, 200 ft gain but progresses at inches per minute through slide alder thicket
pitch_detail.pitch: 3: Fisher Creek to Douglas Creek (off-trail bushwhack)

pitch_detail.notes: 1-2 miles, ~3,000 ft gain, open forest transitioning to scree/rock

pitch_detail.grade: Glacier AI2, steep sections requiring crampons
pitch_detail.notes: Roped team travel, crevasses significant, steep ice sections in upper glacier
~300 vertical feet from glacier col, rock quality solid, exposure significant
Old road walk plus climbers' path from lower to upper Hardscrabble Lake, staying near the inlet.
Ascends from upper Hardscrabble Lake to the col; can hold snow.
Open granite slab below the ridge, then follow the east ridge to the summit.
pitch_detail.pitch: North slope slab to east ridge

pitch_detail.notes: Climb straight up ~450 ft left (east) of the large boulder field, then angle left for ~200 ft to gain the northwest ridgeline.
pitch_detail.pitch: Highway turnout (~1,900 ft) to NW ridge crest

pitch_detail.notes: Cliff bands negotiated via snow ramps in winter/spring; snowshoes typically go on around 4,000 ft.
pitch_detail.pitch: NW Ridge over Point 6315' to ~5,400 ft

pitch_detail.notes: Ridge opens up with mixed rock/snow scrambling.
pitch_detail.pitch: ~5,400 ft transition to West Ridge, to summit ridge (~7,100 ft)

pitch_detail.notes: Final ~300 ft of gain requires scrambling.
pitch_detail.pitch: Summit ridge to true summit (7,426 ft)

pitch_detail.notes: ~7 mi, gains to 4,800 ft camp
pitch_detail.pitch: Sol Duc TH to Heart Lake

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the Cat Basin trail east from the High Divide toward Cat Peak and Cat Basin; no water beyond Heart Lake
Narrow rock/heather ridge connecting Cat Peak to the Bailey Range; a fall could be fatal
Grass, scree and broken shale to the true summit; early-season snow may require an ice axe
